title: SQL Injection via Unsanitized Dynamic Parameter Names in Table.Insert
analysis:
Dapper.Rainbow's `Table<T, TId>.Insert` and `Table<T, TId>.Update` methods dynamically build SQL statements using parameter/column names obtained via `GetParamNames(o)`. When passed an instance of `DynamicParameters`, `GetParamNames` directly extracts parameter names via `parameters.ParameterNames.ToList()`. 

Source: Untrusted user input can populate parameter names when dynamic parameter dictionaries or schema-flexible inputs (e.g., from web API JSON payloads or query parameters) are supplied to `Table.Insert` or `Table.Update`.
Validation/Sanitization: Neither `DynamicParameters` nor `Table<T, TId>.Insert`/`Update` validates or escapes column/parameter names (no square bracket escaping `[name]` or regex validation against identifier syntax).
Sink: Parameter names are concatenated directly into the raw SQL query string (`cols = string.Join(",", paramNames)` and `sql = "set nocount on insert " + TableName + " (" + cols + ") values (" + colsParams + ") select cast(scope_identity() as int)"`), which is executed via `database.Query<int?>(sql, o)`.

Conceptual Exploit Payload:
An attacker sends a JSON request with a malicious property name:
```json
{
  "ValidCol": 1,
  "Foo) VALUES (1); DROP TABLE Users; --": 2
}
```
When parsed into a `DynamicParameters` collection and passed to `table.Insert(dynamicParams)`:
`paramNames` contains `"Foo) VALUES (1); DROP TABLE Users; --"`, producing:
`set nocount on insert MyTable (ValidCol,Foo) VALUES (1); DROP TABLE Users; --) values (@ValidCol,@Foo) VALUES (1); DROP TABLE Users; --) select cast(scope_identity() as int)`
which executes the injected SQL commands.
vuln_type: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection')
